newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM orders investigation into killings.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM orders investigation into killings.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Thursday he had ordered an investigation into the killing of two members of his royalist FUNCINPEC party.
"I am very sorry about this and I have ordered the authorised ministry to investigate," he told reporters.
A police official, who asked not to be named, said that two activists of the FUNCINPEC party were murdered in separate incidents in the past week in Kandal province, which neighbours the capital.

On November 28, Chan Cheoun, a district chief of the FUNCINPEC party, was shot five times. And on December 2, a man was bludgeoned to death with an axe, the policeman said. He did not know the name of the second victim.
The official said the killings were believed to be political, and a spokesperson for the Ministry of Interior said an investigation had been launched.
The news of the murders follows weeks of rising tensions between Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and co-Premier Hun Sen's formerly communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP).

The two leaders, who formed an uneasy coalition government following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, have been at odds over issues ranging from power sharing to the recruitment of defecting Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
